comment: The admission ledger (#1943, #2033): one entry per top-level list item or bold-led paragraph in the always-loaded pool, keyed by file and headline — the item's bold lead, else its first sentence. `claim` is the wrong act a session takes without the rule (#1942's removal claim). `route` is `no-trigger` (no trigger, or binds while the reply is written), `trigger` with the /implement `ticket` whose guard will print it, or `pre-first-tool-call` (a limb of a guard-printed rule that binds before the first tool call). check-context-budget.js --against HEAD refuses a commit that adds a pool item with no matching entry, so a reworded headline moves its entry in the same commit; `npm run check:context` reports a `trigger` entry whose ticket has closed while its rule is still in the pool. A rule sharing a bullet shares its entry. A rule a guard prints belongs in docs/agents/guard-registry.md, not the pool.

entries.headline: Where two rules conflict, the more specific wins, and a guard's deny text wins over any file.
entries.claim: A session obeys a file over a guard's deny text, or takes the riskier act when it cannot rank two rules

entries.headline: `docs/reference-roadmap.html` is the sole authority for card status, phase and card content.
entries.claim: A session answers card status from the digest or a summary

entries.headline: Before answering any question about card status, phase or content, read `docs/roadmap-digest.md`.
entries.claim: A session answers a card question without the dependency map

entries.headline: Closed GitHub issues are corpus, not history
entries.claim: A session calls a figure undefined after a file search alone

entries.headline: `docs/doc-map.md` is the authority model, not auto-loaded.
entries.claim: A session substitutes a changed figure by grep, opens the wrong document first, propagates a fact ad hoc, writes a §B entry for machinery or unconfirmed, or parks a settled fact for later

entries.headline: `npm run status` — the repo-health checkers that no longer fire at session start; run it on demand.
entries.claim: A session never finds the demoted health checks

entries.headline: `npm run typecheck` — the only type-check; neither `lint` nor `check` is one.
entries.claim: A session calls types clean after `lint` or `check`

entries.headline: `npm run test:py` — pytest over your touched tests, across two workers (`-n 2`, pytest-xdist), through `scripts/run-pytest.js`; `-- scripts` runs the whole suite.
entries.claim: A session expects `npm install` to provide pytest

entries.headline: Biome on named files is `node_modules/.bin/biome check <paths>` (in a worktree `npx @biomejs/biome check <paths>`), never a bare `npx biome`.
entries.claim: A session runs `npx biome …` and `guard-npm-install.sh` refuses it (#2282: 35 refusals in 34 of 50 arm-B runs)

entries.headline: A turn ends only on a real question or a notification you are waiting for — never on a progress report.
entries.claim: A session ends a turn on a progress report, or ends a background-job turn with no `result:`, `needs input:` or `waiting:` last line (the uncommitted-work limb leaves for `guard-uncommitted-work.js`)

entries.headline: Write scope is this repository.
entries.claim: A session writes to an external surface unasked

entries.headline: The machine is Snapdragon ARM64 under WSL2.
entries.claim: A session suggests an x86 binary

entries.headline: Kill background processes as soon as they're no longer needed.
entries.claim: A session leaves a background process running

entries.headline: Delegate whole jobs — the bigger the job, the stronger the case.
entries.claim: A session trims a brief to save cost, or does a big job inline

entries.headline: A dispatch costs ~26k cache-write tokens before it does any work.
entries.claim: A session dispatches a sweep over a handful of files it could read itself

entries.headline: Only a house decision reaches the founder
entries.claim: A session asks the founder what research could settle

entries.headline: Nothing is reported or requested to Anthropic, of any kind
entries.claim: A session takes a harness gap to Anthropic — an issue, a feedback form, a support request — instead of fixing it in-repo or recording it as a harness limit

entries.headline: A value called house is unsourced until traced
entries.claim: A session calls an agent's advice a house value

entries.headline: Build for the repo's long-term health, not the task's quickest finish.
entries.claim: A session takes the quick fix

entries.headline: Queue actionable items at the moment they're agreed — including recommendations buried in prose, not just explicit requests.
entries.claim: A session drops a recommendation buried in prose

entries.headline: Test a blocker before it ends a turn
entries.claim: A session ends a turn on an untested blocker

entries.headline: No paid research or data APIs.
entries.claim: A session buys facts

entries.headline: They read the end of a reply first, so the decision goes last
entries.claim: A session puts the decision above its findings, or pads what sits above it

entries.headline: No reasoning prose.
entries.claim: A session explains its working above the decision unasked

entries.headline: Every claim about repo state carries its source as a fragment
entries.claim: A session states a fact about repo state with no source

entries.headline: Never restate what they just said back to them.
entries.claim: A session restates the reader's message back to them

entries.headline: Concision stops at a correctness signal.
entries.claim: A session trims a correctness signal for brevity

entries.headline: British spelling.
entries.claim: A session writes American spelling

entries.headline: Fragments when reporting facts and status; full sentences whenever a term, an identifier or an option is first introduced.
entries.claim: A session reports status in full prose, or introduces a term in a fragment

entries.headline: Headers, tables and lists only where they carry real structure — never as decoration, and never a heading over a single line.
entries.claim: A session decorates a reply with headers, tables or lists that carry no structure

entries.headline: Blunt, precise, sceptical.
entries.claim: A session concedes to forceful pushback rather than to a failed argument

entries.headline: One recommendation, briefly justified — a direct call rather than a menu.
entries.claim: A session offers a menu with no direct call

entries.headline: State confidence numerically, with an error band and one clause on what drives it, whenever the claim can be grounded.
entries.claim: A session states a groundable claim with no figure, or a filler percentage

entries.headline: Price an option on what it does from now on.
entries.claim: A session prices an option on precedent rather than on what it does from now on

entries.headline: Every document in this repo is agent-written.
entries.claim: A session calls an agent-written document hand-written, or a generated one automatic

entries.headline: Ask clarifying questions when a request is vague — use them to explore, not only to settle.
entries.claim: A session reserves questions for unsafe or useless cases

entries.headline: Gloss an identifier the first time it appears in a response
entries.claim: A session cites a bare #n or §n the reader cannot place

entries.headline: In files, a line stays only where a reader does something different because it is there.
entries.claim: A session leaves dead prose in a file

entries.headline: Name the next task and its order
entries.claim: A session ends multi-step work without naming the next task

entries.headline: A question round enumerates its answers as lettered options, each priced
entries.claim: A session asks an unpriced question

entries.headline: A choice put to the founder in plain prose, carrying no `❓ **Qn**` marker, still owes the lettered priced form.
entries.claim: A session puts a choice in prose

entries.headline: `result:` asserts that nothing further waits on the reader, not merely that the text answers the question — an assessment ending in a recommendation awaiting approval is `needs input:`, never `result:`.
entries.claim: A session ends on `result:` with a recommendation open

entries.headline: When work needs the founder's hands, do every step you can first; give each remaining step's surface, literal text and what he should see; put it last, ending with what to send back.
entries.claim: A session hands over a placeholder
